An audit para is a formal audit observation; paras are settled through compliance, recovery or regularisation. q: Which estimate is prepared when it is certain that the work cannot be completed within sanctioned cost?
e: The correct answer is B – Revised Estimate. When it becomes certain that a work cannot be completed within the sanctioned cost, a Revised Estimate is prepared to obtain fresh sanction for the higher cost. A supplementary demand is sought when the sanctioned provision proves inadequate or new expenditure becomes necessary during the year. Remember: Eliminate the distractors first — each wrong option usually describes a related but different concept.

q: What is ceiling limit for each Out of Turn Work sanctioned by GM?
e: The correct answer is B – 2.5 crores. The ceiling limit for each out-of-turn work sanctioned by the GM is Rs. 2.5 crores. This is a concept-clarity question. The right option follows directly from the definition; the wrong ones look plausible only with an approximate recall. Tighten the definition in your revision notes. q: Whose sanction is required to incur expenditure on works of urgent nature costing upto Rs.10 lakhs per case?
e: DRMADRM — that is the right answer. Sanction to incur expenditure on works of an urgent nature costing up to Rs. 10 lakhs per case is given by the DRM. This delegation lets divisions respond quickly to urgent situations without waiting for higher authority. Works beyond this limit escalate to the GM and above. The principle behind this is worth grasping, not just memorising: once you understand why the rule is framed this way, the answer follows naturally instead of needing rote recall.

q: What is ERP system followed in all the production units and workshops of IR?
e: The correct answer is B – the ERP (Enterprise Resource Planning) system. All production units and workshops of Indian Railways follow an ERP system, which integrates planning, materials, production and finance functions on a common platform. The key is the precise meaning the question tests: each option describes a closely related but distinct idea, and only one fits the definition exactly. In the exam, such questions reward careful reading of definitions — compare every option against the textbook meaning word by word.

q: In RITES Incentive Scheme which shop is eligible for Incentive?
e: The correct answer is B – Direct Shops. Under the RITES Incentive Scheme, only direct shops (production shops directly engaged in the output) are eligible for incentive. Incentive schemes pay workers extra for output above a standard, linking earnings to productivity while protecting a guaranteed time wage. q: Workshop Outturn Register is posted every month from
e: The correct answer is B – Workshop General Register. The Workshop Outturn Register is posted every month from the Workshop General Register, which is the primary record of work done in the workshop. Outturn is the measured output of a workshop (completed repairs/manufacture) valued for costing and performance comparison. Remember: Make a one-line note of this concept for revision; it recurs in several papers.

q: Important Performance Unit for expenditure under Demand No.5C Repairs & Maintenance of Motive Power is
e: The correct answer is Engine Holdings. The important performance unit for expenditure under Demand No. 5C (Repairs and Maintenance of Motive Power) is engine holdings, i.e. the number of engines held on the railway. Expenditure on motive power maintenance is meaningfully compared per engine held. Number of engines, equated track kms and engine hours are not the prescribed unit for this demand. This provision exists for a practical reason in day-to-day railway working; keeping that practical picture in mind makes the fact far easier to retain than memorising it in isolation.

q: Important Performance Unit for expenditure under Demand No.8F Operating Expenses Rolling Stock & Equipment
e: No. of Running Staff — that is the right answer. of Running Staff. The important performance unit for expenditure under Demand No. 8F (Operating Expenses – Rolling Stock and Equipment) is the number of running staff. Running staff costs dominate this operating demand, so expenditure is assessed per running staff member. GTKMs, number of engines and equated track kms are units for other demands. A useful way to verify this in the exam hall is to ask what would break if the opposite were true — the logic of the underlying system points straight to this option.

q: What is CSER prepared by ICAIIARF?
e: The correct answer is Comprehensive Scope Evaluation Report. CSER stands for Comprehensive Scope Evaluation Report, prepared in connection with the costing system evaluation work associated with ICAI/ARF. It evaluates the scope of the costing system rather than being a computerised study or earnings report. The expansion itself is the key exam fact here. The principle behind this is worth grasping, not just memorising: once you understand why the rule is framed this way, the answer follows naturally instead of needing rote recall.

q: Track Fittings are purchased by
e: Option A (Engineering Department) is the correct choice. Track fittings are purchased by the Engineering Department, since permanent way materials fall under the engineering branch's responsibility. The Stores Department arranges procurement, but the indenting and technical responsibility for track fittings lies with Engineering. Mechanical and Traffic departments do not deal with track fittings. Notice how precisely the correct option is worded. The paper tests exact scope here, not an approximate idea, which is why careful reading of the question stem matters.

q: Purchase of imported WTA items is handled by
e: The correct answer is Railway Board. The purchase of imported WTA items is handled by the Railway Board, keeping centralised control over foreign procurement. Imported wheel/tyre/axle items involve foreign exchange and specialised sourcing, which is why the decision rests at the Board level rather than with RWF, ICF or the GM. Centralised handling also ensures uniform policy on imports. This provision exists for a practical reason in day-to-day railway working; keeping that practical picture in mind makes the fact far easier to retain than memorising it in isolation.
